prompt: A hand-painted world map for a premium world-conquest board game, top-down, filling the frame. Use the reference only for palette and layout; the rendering must go clearly BEYOND it toward a real illustrator's gouache-and-ink original photographed flat. Deep indigo handmade paper with visible fibres and slight uneven tone. Coastlines drawn in silver-ivory ink with a real brush: line weight swells and thins, occasional dry-brush breaks, small ink pools where strokes begin, a few coastal islands dotted with the brush tip. Territories are translucent pigment washes (muted vermilion, slate blue, ochre, sage) laid wet: granulation, soft blooms and back-runs, darker tide lines where the wash dried, paper grain showing through. Territory borders are thin hand-drawn ivory lines, slightly irregular. Ocean: bare indigo paper, a few sparse swell strokes and a faint breath of pale mist. Small ivory ink rings with serif numerals mark army counts on each territory. Restraint above all: no title, no words, no compass rose, no ships, no sun, no kanji, no seals, no blossoms, no UI.
